text:
Alex Chen: FYI — escalation from customer `MapleMaps` (ticket #4952). They report intermittent 429s + tail latency spikes on our geocoding route `/v1/geocode` starting ~03:10 UTC. They attached a sample request and a correlation id `cid:abc123`.

InfraBot: automated alert — RateLimiter: bucket drop detected for route=/v1/geocode tenant=t-942 window=60s qps=250 p99_latency=1200ms throttle_rate=18% (alert_id: rl-20230310-01) :rotating_light:

Maria Gomez: quick look at logs — lots of perfectly parallel requests from a single API key (sdk-js v2.3.1). Requests are tiny (single-address lookups) so we get high qps. Sample log lines:
```
2026-03-10T03:11:05Z INFO req_id=abc123 tenant=t-942 route=/v1/geocode size=78ms qps_token=1
2026-03-10T03:11:05Z WARN req_id=abc124 tenant=t-942 route=/v1/geocode status=429 reason=rate_limited
```

Samir Patel: probable cause = burst exhaustion of tenant bucket + our per-route microburst threshold. Two immediate remediation options:
- ask customer to implement client-side concurrency limits / exponential backoff
- temporarily increase tenant burst allowance or create a per-tenant override

Evelyn (support): I already asked the customer for exact SDK version, timestamps, and a short repro script. They sent curl snippet:
```
for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." https://api.redwood.ai/v1/geocode -d '{"q":"123 Main St"}' &
done
```

Alex Chen: creating a temporary per-tenant override (t-942) to raise burst window from 60s -> 120s and bump burst tokens by +50%. Will monitor for 15m. Also enabling a per-route fallback to the smaller model so we keep latency bounded if the main worker pool hits queueing.

Maria Gomez: dashboard snapshots — linking live views: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/rl?route=%2Fv1%2Fgeocode&tenant=t-942 and grafana panel: https://grafana.internal/redwood/dashboard/db/rate-limiter — see spike at 03:10 and the throttle percentage climb. Alert rule rl-20230310-01 fired at 03:12.

Samir Patel: if override works, we should also update our observability to show "throttled_by" attribution on the tenant-level timeline. Current gap: when a route fallback occurs we don't always tag the 429 with the model variant. That makes postmortem attribution messy.

Evelyn (support): Customer is ok with temporary override if we confirm billing impact. Maria — can you estimate token consumption delta for the 15m override? They are on usage plan with soft quota.

Maria Gomez: estimate = +8k tokens over 15m at current QPS. Not huge, but FYI customer will get charged under current plan. I'll add a note to the ticket.

InfraBot: mitigation applied: tenant_override t-942 applied by AlexChen at 03:16 UTC. Monitoring window open.

Alex Chen: monitoring — p95 dropped from 900ms -> 320ms after override, throttle% down to 4%. Leaving override for 15m then plan to roll back. Next steps:
- Evelyn: notify customer + confirm they add client-side concurrency limit
- Samir: file infra task to add model-variant tagging for throttles (priority medium)
- Maria: create short-run dashboard showing "throttled_by: tenant|route|model" and add a playbook snippet for on-call

Evelyn (support): will update ticket and ask them to test with sdk-js v2.4.0 (has client-side retry helper). Also asked for repro script that respects Retry-After and backoff.

Samir Patel: note for postmortem — investigate whether our prefix/KV-cache warmup could have amplified qps (cold cache generating more compute per request). If so, we should surface cache-warmup indicators on the rate-limiter dashboard.

Alex Chen: thanks team. If anything regresses I'll reopen this thread. For now, leaving open until override rolled back and customer confirms.

Evelyn (support): marked ticket #4952 as "mitigated — monitoring" and set follow-up for 2026-03-10 03:35 UTC.
__notes: Slack thread; no title field per agents.md
